ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
An object with a mass of $0.5\mathrm{kg}$ falls freely from a height and hits the ground after 4 seconds, with the gravitational acceleration $g=10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$.

1. Find the displacement of the object within 2 seconds from the start of the fall.
2. Find the work done by gravity within the first 2 seconds of falling.
3. Find the momentum of the object just as it reaches the ground.

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: An object with a mass of $0.5\mathrm{kg}$ falls freely from a height and hits the ground after 4 seconds, with the gravitational acceleration $g=10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$. 1. Find the displacement of the object within 2 seconds from the start of the fall. 2. Find the work done by gravity within the first 2 seconds of falling. 3. Find the momentum of the object just as it reaches the ground.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Given mass m = 0.5 kg, gravitational acceleration g = 10 m/s^2, total fall time T = 4 s, and the object is in free fall from rest. For the first 2 s, use the free-fall displacement formula s = (1/2)gt^2. With t = 2 s, s = (1/2)(10)(2^2) = 5 × 4 = 20 m. The gravitational force is F = mg = 0.5 × 10 = 5 N. The work done by gravity during the first 2 s is W = Fs = 5 × 20 = 100 J. Just before reaching the ground after 4 s, the speed is v = gT = 10 × 4 = 40 m/s. The momentum is p = mv = 0.5 × 40 = 20 kg·m/s.
